title:
A symbol ending with a number is made invisible when printing with MathML
A variable with a number,

observations: Symbols ending with a number (e.g., x2) become invisible when printed as MathML (presentation format).
Example: expression x2*z + x2**3 renders invisibly in Safari.
Symbols without trailing numbers (e.g., x) render correctly.
Bug demonstrated with SymPy 1.3, Python 3.7, macOS 10.14.2, Safari 12.0.2.
Code snippet uses sympy.printing.mathml.mathml with printer='presentation'.
Output saved to HTML file and viewed in browser; screenshot shows missing x2.
Reproduction steps are clear: create symbol ending with digit, generate MathML, view in browser.
c1_text.causal_hypothesis: The MathML presentation printer likely generates an invalid element (e.g., <mi> tag with incorrect content or attributes) for symbols ending with digits, causing browsers to not render them.

title:
Wrong legend values of large ranges
As of 0.12.1, legends describing large numbers that were created

observations: Bug title: 'Wrong legend values of large ranges'
Version: As of 0.12.1
Issue: Legends describing large numbers created using ScalarFormatter with an offset are formatted without their multiplicative offset value
Example: Plot with variable 'body_mass_mg' (order 1E6) shows legend values without offset (e.g., 3000 instead of 3e6?)
Reproduces with seaborn.objects (so.Plot) and scatterplot
Referenced code lines: seaborn/_core/scales.py lines 377-382
Issue depends on matplotlib rcParams: axes.formatter.useoffset, axes.formatter.offset_threshold
Offset value can be retrieved from formatters and used for legend title/labels
c1_text.causal_hypothesis: The legend generation code in seaborn's scales.py does not incorporate the offset value from ScalarFormatter when formatting legend labels for large numbers, causing labels to display raw scaled values instead of the offset-applied representation.
